threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You can always tell the newbies by how they can't differentiate a 'Boris bike' from a Santander cycle. We see you, it's cute.
Last night on the 50, a passenger tried to convince the driver to play his mixtape. Never seen someone so determined to get their tunes heard at 3 AM.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a guy casually repairing his bike while a busker played tango near the canal, I knew this place was special.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a Kebab shop that doubles as an art gallery. Late-night snacks and local art collide in the most unexpected ways.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local when they know to avoid BART during rush hour after a loud bang; the panic's palpable but they’re already strategizing their next move.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a guy juggling on the 47. One hand had a coffee, the other a half-eaten burrito. Only in SF do we multi-task like that.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about the bars, but the real gem is the local markets where the true rhythm of life beats.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by the way they struggle to open the trash bins; locals have mastered the foot pedal technique long ago.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it a 'trolley' instead of a 'shopping trolley' and look confused when locals say 'bag for life'.
Caught a late 133 last night, overheard a group debating the merits of jellied eels. Only in Brixton, right?

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I remember the day I spotted a group of kids using an old tire as a makeshift basketball hoop in a random park. That's when it hit me—this place has character.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain do you find a hidden bar in a laundromat where DJs spin vinyl while you wait for your spin cycle.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know you’re a local when you can spot the tourists trying to figure out how to cross 24th without getting run over by a bus.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a guy serenading Muni riders with a ukulele during the morning rush. Only in San Francisco would folks break into spontaneous applause between stops.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists flock to Park Güell but miss the hidden murals on the back streets of Gràcia. The real soul of the barrio is in the small plazas and local cafés.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their wide-eyed wonder at the simplest street performers, while locals just walk past without a glance.
